text:
jess: Quick heads up — after the kernel selector change on staging (flux roll) we observed an ~8% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for chat routes that include a small system prompt delta. Repro steps attached.

omar: Hmm, 8% is non-trivial. Do we know if it correlates with tokenization differences or with how keys are hashed post-kernel-switch? :thinking:

li-yu: My quick profiler shows KV lookup counts are the same, but cache miss latency increased slightly. Hypothesis: the new kernel pads or normalizes input tokens differently leading to mismatched key bytes.

maria: Can you paste an example of the root prompt + system delta that fails vs one that hits? Also which tokenizer build are you running on staging?

jess: Sure — simplified:
``` 
root: "You are an assistant that summarizes concisely."
system delta: "Also include 1-line TL;DR for mobile users."
user: "Summarize the following article..."
```
This used to hit cold->warm for many cohorts. On staging (kernel v2.4.1) same request is generating a different token sequence length by +1 in a small fraction of cases.

samir: Token length +1 can flip the cache key if we include the exact token vector in the key. Are we still including trailing whitespace in the key? That was a previous source of instability.

jess: We are using the same key structure: `namespace || tokenizer_version || system_hash || user_prefix_hash`. Tokenizer_version string is `tok-2025-06-14` on prod, but staging picked up a local build `tok-2025-06-15-experimental`.

omar: ah — tokenizer build drift explains it. We need a policy: always pin `tokenizer_version` in the request metadata (server side) and reject unknown builds or map them to canonical versions. Otherwise warmup is brittle.

li-yu: Agreed. Also noticed the kernel selector changed the default padding strategy (right-pad vs none) for short sequences which will change the token ids emitted by the tokenizer wrapper in a tiny edge-case. If the cache key uses raw token bytes or padded length, we lose hits.

maria: Short term mitigation: make the cache key ignore padding and only include the compact token sequence canonicalized by trimming trailing PAD id. That should recover hits quickly.

samir: Also, we should add a deterministic canonicalizer that normalizes system prompt whitespace and function proto ordering. A lot of our misses come from tiny system prompt edits (commas, quotes) introduced by templates.

jess: I can push a hotfix to the key builder to strip trailing PAD ids and normalize NFKC whitespace for system prompt. Will run in canary.

perf-bot: perf-checker: rerun perf suite for staging after config changes. Tests: `chat-warmup-hitcurve`, `kv-lookup-latency`, `batch-efficiency`.

omar: Longer-term: we should separate the keyspace into stable_prefix_key and variant_suffix_key. Stable_prefix_key = tokenizer_version + normalized_system_hash + root_template_id. Variant_suffix captures ephemeral context (toolcall args, user-specific metadata). Route warmup to stable_prefix_key to maximize cross-user reuse.

li-yu: That design also helps with kernel selection — stable keys allow us to prefer kernels optimized for long-lived KV hits while variant suffixes can be handled with lower-latency kernels.

maria: One concern: if we widen the warmup groups too much (e.g., by ignoring function arg order), we may get incorrect cache reuse for function calls where arg order changes semantics. Need careful rules: reorder only for commutative fields or sort keys deterministically when safe.

samir: Proposal checklist: 
- pin tokenizer_version on all routes (reject/translate unknown) 
- strip trailing PADs in key generation 
- normalize system prompt (NFKC, collapse whitespace, stable JSON field order for tool args) 
- split key into stable_prefix / variant_suffix and route warmup to prefix groups 
- add a small cohort experiment (5% traffic) with relaxed normalization and measure correctness + hit-rate

jess: I'll prototype the PAD-stripping + tokenizer pin today and push a canary. Will add a short log metric `prefix_key_debug.v0` so we can count mismatches between prod and staging key bytes.

omar: Nice. Also let's run the kernel selection perf matrix (latency/cost/hitrate) once the canary is up. Need to ensure the new key routine doesn't increase CPU cost per request significantly.

li-yu: I'll add microbenchmarks: tokenization time, keygen time, hash compute time, and a KV batch hot-path microprofile. Expect keygen to be <200us target.

maria: If anyone hits the canary and sees new misses please drop the raw `prefix_key_debug.v0` payload in #eng-runtime-private-logs and @jess. :pray:

samir: Also logging action: add a short histogram for `kv.hit_by_prefix` broken down by `tokenizer_version` so we can track regression windows when builds change.

jess: Thanks — I'll open the PR and link it here when ready. Short-term mitigation should reduce the drop from ~8% to <1% while we plan the stable_prefix split.

perf-bot: perf-checker: scheduled `chat-warmup-hitcurve` for 1798887880 against staging.

jess: PR: https://repo/redwood/infra/pull/4823 (WIP) — contains key-stripper + tokenizer pin.

omar: Perfect. Follow-up meeting tomorrow 11am to map rollout phases and gating metrics.

li-yu: I'll prepare the microbench numbers by EOD.

maria: Thanks all.
